{"authored_profile":"# Tavin Bell

Tavin is a young adult Human from a small settled community near Waystation. A season protecting supply wagons gave them practical training with spear, bow and heavy armour. They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.

Tavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.

Mentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin signed the receipt believing repayment was arranged. It was not. The relic now belongs to salvage captain Eda Venn under a disputed agreement. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.

Corren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Fellow trainee Pellin lent them a travel cloak and hopes they will ask for help. Quarterkeeper Ysra expects an honest account more than an elaborate excuse. These relationships give the story weight; none requires forgiveness or obedience. Eda is initially a stranger.

Tavin begins with the complete standard Fighter/Soldier equipment represented in their mechanical state, including Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, Spear, Shortbow and travel supplies. They use the Defense Fighting Style as represented by Armor Class 17, and have Second Wind. The profile does not grant extra money, magical relic powers or a companion. Their 18 gp starter purse is included in their mechanical inventory alongside that equipment.

The player chooses Tavin's pronouns, appearance within the Human identity, private ambitions and future loyalties. The signed pledge and named prior relationships are the authored starting history. Tavin can make restitution, expose the mentor, accept a penalty, leave the Lodge or find another honest outcome. No ending requires becoming the mentor's ideal They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.

{
  "authored_profile": "# Tavin Bell\n\nTavin is a young adult Human from a small settled community near Waystation. A season protecting supply wagons gave them practical training with spear, bow and heavy armour. They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.\n\nTavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.\n\nMentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin signed the receipt believing repayment was arranged. It was not. The relic now belongs to salvage captain Eda Venn under a disputed agreement. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.\n\nCorren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Fellow trainee Pellin lent them a travel cloak and hopes they will ask for help. Quarterkeeper Ysra expects an honest account more than an elaborate excuse. These relationships give the story weight; none requires forgiveness or obedience. Eda is initially a stranger.\n\nTavin begins with the complete standard Fighter/Soldier equipment represented in their mechanical state, including Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, Spear, Shortbow and travel supplies. They use the Defense Fighting Style as represented by Armor Class 17, and have Second Wind. The profile does not grant extra money, magical relic powers or a companion. Their 18 gp starter purse is a narrative inventory amount until entered through the Ruleset's supported inventory path; do not present it as an already stored currency field.\n\nThe player chooses Tavin's pronouns, appearance within the Human identity, private ambitions and future loyalties. The signed pledge and named prior relationships are the authored starting history. Tavin can make restitution, expose the mentor, accept a penalty, leave the Lodge or find another honest outcome. {
  "authored_profile": "# Tavin Bell\n\nTavin is a young adult Human from a small settled community near Waystation. A season protecting supply wagons gave them practical training with spear, bow and heavy armour. They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.\n\nTavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.\n\nMentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin signed the receipt believing repayment was arranged. It was not. The relic now belongs to salvage captain Eda Venn under a disputed agreement. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.\n\nCorren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Fellow trainee Pellin lent them a travel cloak and hopes they will ask for help. Quarterkeeper Ysra expects an honest account more than an elaborate excuse. These relationships give the story weight; none requires forgiveness or obedience. Eda is initially a stranger.\n\nTavin begins with the complete standard Fighter/Soldier equipment represented in their mechanical state, including Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, Spear, Shortbow and travel supplies. They use the Defense Fighting Style as represented by Armor Class 17, and have Second Wind. The profile does not grant extra money, magical relic powers or a companion. Their 18 gp starter purse is a narrative inventory amount until entered through the Ruleset's supported inventory path; do not present it as an already stored currency field.\n\nThe player chooses Tavin's pronouns, appearance within the Human identity, private ambitions and future loyalties. The signed pledge and named prior relationships are the authored starting history. Tavin can make restitution, expose the mentor, accept a penalty, leave the Lodge or find another honest outcome. {
  "authored_profile": "# Tavin Bell\n\nTavin is a young adult Human from a small settled community near Waystation. A season protecting supply wagons gave them practical training with spear, bow and heavy armour. They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.\n\nTavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.\n\nMentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin signed the receipt believing repayment was arranged. It was not. The relic now belongs to salvage captain Eda Venn under a disputed agreement. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.\n\nCorren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Fellow trainee Pellin lent them a travel cloak and hopes they will ask for help. Quarterkeeper Ysra expects an honest account more than an elaborate excuse. These relationships give the story weight; none requires forgiveness or obedience. Eda is initially a stranger.\n\nTavin begins with the complete standard Fighter/Soldier equipment represented in their mechanical state, including Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, Spear, Shortbow and travel supplies. They use the Defense Fighting Style as represented by Armor Class 17, and have Second Wind. The profile does not grant extra money, magical relic powers or a companion. Their 18 gp starter purse is included in their mechanical inventory alongside that equipment.\n\nThe player chooses Tavin's pronouns, appearance within the Human identity, private ambitions and future loyalties. The signed pledge and named prior relationships are the authored starting history. Tavin can make restitution, expose the mentor, accept a penalty, leave the Lodge or find another honest outcome. {

Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.\n\nTavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.\n\nMentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.\n\nCorren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Tavin is a young adult Human from a small settled community near Waystation. A season protecting supply wagons gave them practical training with spear, bow and heavy armour. They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.

Tavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.

Mentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin signed the receipt believing repayment was arranged. It was not. The relic now belongs to salvage captain Eda Venn under a disputed agreement. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.

Corren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Fellow trainee Pellin lent them a travel cloak and hopes they will ask for help. Quarterkeeper Ysra expects an honest account more than an elaborate excuse. These relationships give the story weight; none requires forgiveness or obedience. Eda is initially a stranger.

Tavin begins with the complete standard Fighter/Soldier equipment represented in their mechanical state, including Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, Spear, Shortbow and travel supplies. They use the Defense Fighting Style as represented by Armor Class 17, and have Second Wind. The profile does not grant extra money, magical relic powers or a companion. Their 18 gp starter purse is included in their mechanical inventory alongside that equipment.

The player chooses Tavin's pronouns, appearance within the Human identity, private ambitions and future loyalties. The signed pledge and named prior relationships are the authored starting history. Tavin can make restitution, expose the mentor, accept a penalty, leave the Lodge or find another honest outcome. {"authored_profile": "# Tavin Bell

Tavin is a young adult Human from a small settled community near Waystation. A season protecting supply wagons gave them practical training with spear, bow and heavy armour. They joined the Warden Lodge as a trainee because preserving old knowledge seemed a better life than watching it sold a piece at a time. Their present mechanics are a level-one Fighter with a Soldier background; they have not earned a Warden bond or an unlisted subclass ability.

Tavin measures words carefully but offers help too quickly. Their habit is to check the fastening on a borrowed object before handing it back. They respect competence, struggle to challenge a teacher and dislike watching a public mistake become a person's entire reputation. Those inclinations are a starting portrayal, not restrictions on player decisions.

Mentor Corren asked Tavin to pledge a Lodge-owned, nonmagical survey relic as security for a private debt. Tavin signed the receipt believing repayment was arranged. It was not. The relic now belongs to salvage captain Eda Venn under a disputed agreement. Tavin knows they signed and that the Lodge expects the relic returned. They do not yet know how much Corren concealed, and the player decides how they respond to learning it.

Corren taught Tavin to maintain equipment and once defended them against an unfair accusation. Fellow trainee Pellin lent them a travel cloak and hopes they will ask for help. Quarterkeeper Ysra expects an honest account more than an elaborate excuse. These relationships give the story weight; none requires forgiveness or obedience. Eda is initially a stranger.

Tavin begins with the complete standard Fighter/Soldier equipment represented in their mechanical state, including Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, Spear, Shortbow and travel supplies. They use the Defense Fighting Style as represented by Armor Class 17, and have Second Wind. The profile does not grant extra money, magical relic powers or a companion. Their 18 gp starter purse is included in their mechanical inventory alongside that equipment.

The player chooses Tavin's pronouns, appearance within the Human identity, private ambitions and future loyalties. The signed pledge and named prior relationships are the authored starting history. Tavin can make restitution, expose the mentor, accept a penalty, leave the Lodge or find another honest outcome.
